question.text: If a trader's speculative loss from OTC derivatives is Rs. 4 lakhs and speculative income from other OTC trades is Rs. 1 lakh, what is the loss that can be carried forward?

answer.text: Nothing — speculative losses cannot be carried forward

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the Income Tax Act, a speculative business loss can be set off, in the same assessment year, only against speculative business income — it cannot be set off against ordinary business or other heads. So the Rs.4 lakh speculative loss is first set off against the Rs.1 lakh of speculative income from other OTC trades, leaving Rs.3 lakh of unabsorbed speculative loss. That Rs.3 lakh is then carried forward, again to be set off only against speculative business income in subsequent years, for a maximum of 4 assessment years. The Trap: Carrying forward Rs.4 lakh ignores the mandatory same-year set-off against the Rs.1 lakh of speculative income. Carrying forward only Rs.1 lakh inverts which figure gets carried. Saying speculative losses can never be carried forward is incorrect — they can, but only within the speculative bucket and only for 4 assessment years. Note: The cited NISM Series IV Interest Rate Derivatives workbook pages reviewed in the audit cover ETIRD taxation and state speculative losses may be set off only against speculative income, but the OTC-specific speculative-loss carry-forward and the 4-assessment-year period are not on the pages checked. The framing above reflects the general carry-forward rules for speculative business losses under the Income Tax Act.
